questions.stem: Between June and September the landmass of India heats up faster than the surrounding oceans, and moist winds blow in from the Indian Ocean, the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal to bring rainfall; which statement correctly explains why these winds travel in that direction? questions.stem:
On the other side of the year, a school inland in India keeps its own diary of the wind. From October onwards the mornings are cool, and the wind that used to arrive from the sea stops coming. Instead the wind moves away from the land, out towards the seas, and the days stay dry for months together. The children notice the same change recorded in their grandparents' diaries, and they want to know what the land and the sea are doing differently in these colder months.

(a) Name the system of monsoon winds that blows from the land out towards the seas between October and February, and give its other name. (b) State which of the land and the sea lies at high pressure and which lies at low pressure during these months. (c) Explain why the land and the sea behave differently in these cooler months.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) The winter monsoon, also called the north-east monsoon. (b) High pressure lies over the land and low pressure over the seas. (c) The Indian landmass cools faster than the surrounding oceans in this season, so high pressure builds up over the land, and winds then move from the land out towards the seas.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Composition and Structure of the Atmosphere
questions.stem:
A newspaper office keeps a map on its wall, and a reporter is told that the winds which water the fields across the country are not the same for the whole year. These winds are seasonal, and they change with the passing months. The reporter is sent out to find out how many systems of these winds there are, which seas they travel across, and which one of them does most of the work of bringing rain to the farms and villages of the country.

(a) State how many systems of monsoon winds there are and name them. (b) Name the waters across which the system that brings rain between June and September travels. (c) Explain why that system is said to account for most of the rainfall in the country throughout the year.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Two: the south-west and the north-east monsoon. (b) The Indian Ocean, the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal. (c) It blows from sea to land across those waters between June and September, so the moist winds it carries reach the land and bring rainfall, and it accounts for most of the rainfall in the country throughout the year.
